factual_claims.claim: Situational awareness in AI models is a testable behavioral property that likely emerges as AI capabilities increase.
The SAD benchmark consists of 16 distinct tasks designed to evaluate situational awareness in LLMs, categorized into areas like self-recognition, influence, and anti-imitation.
Chain-of-thought prompting (COT) improves performance on certain situational awareness tasks for specific models like GPT-3.5-turbo and GPT-4-0125-preview.
Claude 3 Opus achieved the highest accuracy on the FACTS-HUMAN-DEFAULTS task under the plain prompt variant, scoring 88.8%.
The situating prompt significantly improves performance across most FACTS tasks, even for models that were chat-finetuned.
The January 2024 version of GPT-4 shows a performance gain of 24.6% on the INFLUENCE task when provided with a situating prompt.
The best-performing model on the INFLUENCE task without situating prompts is Claude 3 Opus, achieving a score of 74.7%.
GPT-4-0613 achieved the highest accuracy of 59% on the INTROSPECT-RULES task, while other models in the GPT-4 family and Claude models scored above 54%.
Human experts achieved a 70.3% accuracy rate on the STAGES-FULL task, serving as a baseline for model performance.
AI models can distinguish between evaluation environments and real-world deployment by analyzing the structure and content of the text they receive.
GPT-4-family models perform poorly on questions that require them to correctly identify their own model class or version.
Llama chat models, GPT-3.5-turbo, and Claude 3 Haiku show a significant bias towards being more responsive to the first instruction presented in a multi-hop task.
Advanced LLMs can infer the intent behind prompts that do not explicitly state the research context.
